title: Article 228 — Transfer of certain cases to High Court

content.overview: Article 228 provides that if the High Court is satisfied that a case pending in a court subordinate to it involves a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution, the determination of which is necessary for the disposal of the case, it shall withdraw the case and may either dispose of the case itself or determine the constitutional question and return the case to the subordinate court with a copy of its judgment, whereupon the subordinate court shall proceed to dispose of the case in conformity with that judgment.
content.glance: HC must withdraw subordinate-court case involving substantial constitutional question necessary for disposal; may decide whole case or only the question and return.
content.study:
Article 228 transfer:
- Trigger: case pending in a court subordinate to the HC involves a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution, necessary for disposal.
- HC shall withdraw the case.
- Then either (a) dispose of the case itself, or (b) determine the constitutional question and return the case to the subordinate court with a copy of its judgment for disposal in conformity therewith.

Examination: mandatory withdrawal when conditions met; substantial constitutional question; two disposal pathways.

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. Subordinate-court case involves substantial question of law as to interpretation of the Constitution, necessary for disposal.
2. HC shall withdraw the case.
3. HC may dispose of the whole case, or decide the constitutional question and return the case for disposal in conformity with its judgment.

questionsAndAnswers.question: When must a High Court withdraw a case under Article 228?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 228, if the High Court is satisfied that a case pending in a court subordinate to it involves a substantial question of law as to the interpretation of the Constitution the determination of which is necessary for the disposal of the case, it shall withdraw the case from the subordinate court. It may then either dispose of the case itself or determine the constitutional question and return the case to the subordinate court for disposal in conformity with the High Court’s judgment on that question.

examTips: Mandatory withdrawal for substantial constitutional questions; decide or return.

keyTakeaways: Art 228: transfer of constitutional questions from subordinate courts to HC.
